Features.label: Features
Features.title: Everything you need, {highlight}
Features.subtitle: Replace dozens of {command} commands with an intuitive interface.

screenshot.title: Screen Capture
screenshot.description: Grab clean screenshots from the selected simulator and keep capture settings close to the rest of your testing workflow.

video.title: Recording
video.description: Record simulator sessions without jumping through Terminal commands, then save the result right from the same workspace.

proxy.title: Network Proxy
proxy.description: Inspect requests, introduce delays, simulate failures, and validate edge cases with a built-in proxy workflow.

push.title: Push Payload Testing
push.description: Queue test notifications, preview how they render on-device, and verify custom payload data before shipping.

deeplinks.title: Deep Links
deeplinks.description: Store reusable URL schemes and universal links so common app flows stay one click away during debugging.

gps.title: Locations and Routes
gps.description: Build route presets, replay movement, and coordinate changes across your simulator tests without leaving the panel.

apps.title: Multiple Simulators
apps.description: Run and control more than one simulator from the same workspace while keeping runtime tools, appearance, and app controls close by.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Flip simulator appearance and related UI settings while you test states side by side.

statusbar.title: Status Bar
statusbar.description: Adjust simulator presentation details like status bar output when a test or capture needs a cleaner frame.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.description: Reset and manage app permissions (camera, location, notifications) without reinstalling.

faceid.title: Face ID
faceid.description: Simulate enrollment, match, and mismatch for biometric authentication testing.

keychain.title: Keychain
keychain.description: Browse and manage keychain items stored by your app in the simulator.

profiles.title: App Profiles
profiles.description: Every app keeps its own setup: its bundle ID, its simulators, and the deep links, pushes and locations that belong to it. Switch app, switch everything.

userdefaults.title: UserDefaults Editor
userdefaults.description: Read the app's live defaults, flip a flag, rewrite an array or delete a key, then restart the app from the panel.

diagnostics.title: Scheme Diagnostics
diagnostics.description: Zombies, Main Thread Checker, Core Data SQL logging and 8 more Xcode diagnostics — attached to a profile, not a scheme. Turn them on once, run them every time.

presets.title: Dev Presets
presets.description: Restore a whole working setup in one click instead of rebuilding it by hand every morning.

diskdoctor.title: Disk Doctor
diskdoctor.description: See exactly where your simulator storage went and reclaim the tens of gigabytes old runtimes leave behind.

devices.title: Paired Devices
devices.description: A read-only panel listing the iPhones and iPads paired with your Mac, with model, iOS version and connection state.

menubar.title: Menu Bar
menubar.description: Capture the booted simulator from any app with ⌃⌥⌘S, without switching windows. The menu bar also keeps your last five captures one click away, boots the simulator you used last, and re-sends your most recent push payload.

generator.title: App Store Screenshots
generator.description: Render your captures at the exact sizes the App Store requires, for iPhone, iPad and Mac, without opening a design tool.

ai.title: Works with your AI agent
ai.description: Run cosmokit mcp and any MCP client, such as Claude Code or Cursor, discovers 35 simulator tools it can call with typed arguments: install and launch apps, capture screenshots and video, replay GPS routes, send push payloads, flip permissions, trust a debugging certificate, and read UserDefaults and logs. Every command also takes --json, so an agent that only runs shell still gets a structured result to parse instead of prose.

cli.title: cosmokit CLI
cli.description: The same simulator operations from the terminal, for Makefiles, git hooks and CI. Free, open source, and it runs without the app.

Gallery.title: See it in action
Gallery.subtitle: A native macOS interface designed for speed and clarity.

FAQ.label: FAQ
FAQ.title: Frequently asked questions
FAQ.subtitle: Everything you need to know about CosmoKit.

q1.question: What is CosmoKit?
q1.answer: CosmoKit is a native macOS app that provides a unified control panel for the iOS Simulator. It replaces dozens of terminal commands (xcrun simctl) with an intuitive graphical interface: screenshot capture, video recording, push notifications, deep links, GPS simulation, network proxy, app management, and more.

q2.question: What are the system requirements?
q2.answer: CosmoKit requires macOS 14.7 (Sonoma) or later and Xcode installed on your Mac. It works with all iOS Simulator runtimes supported by your Xcode version.

q3.question: What's included in the free tier?
q3.answer: The free tier includes screenshot and video capture (with watermark), push notifications, deep link testing, GPS location simulation, the simulator tools (appearance, status bar, permissions, Face ID, keychain), the UserDefaults editor, 1 app profile, and 5 saved entries per tool. It supports one simulator at a time.

q4.question: What does CosmoKit Pro unlock?
q4.answer: Pro removes all watermarks, unlocks unlimited simulators and unlimited app profiles, adds device frames and bezels for screenshots, audio recording, touch indicators, custom aspect ratios, network proxy, full app management tools, App Store screenshot generation, location routes, and unlimited saved entries.

q5.question: How does billing work?
q5.answer: All subscriptions are managed through the Mac App Store. You can choose monthly ($2.99/mo, 3-day free trial), yearly ($19.99/yr, save 44%), or a one-time lifetime purchase ($69.99). You can cancel or switch plans anytime through your Apple ID settings. Prices vary by region. The final price is shown in the Mac App Store.

q6.question: Is CosmoKit sandboxed?
q6.answer: Yes, CosmoKit is distributed through the Mac App Store and runs in a sandboxed environment. It communicates with the iOS Simulator through approved system APIs and xcrun simctl commands.

q7.question: Does it work with physical devices?
q7.answer: CosmoKit's tools target the iOS Simulator. Since 4.6 it also shows a read-only Devices panel listing the iPhones and iPads paired with your Mac, with model, iOS version and connection state. Capture, GPS, push and the other tools remain simulator-only.

q8.question: How do I get support?
q8.answer: You can reach us at contato@usecosmoskittool.com or through the in-app feedback option. We actively respond to all support requests and feature suggestions.
